title: QA & Automation Engineering Readiness
description: Assess your skills in automated testing frameworks, Playwright/Selenium, API testing, test case design, and CI/CD quality gates.

questions.question: What is the Page Object Model (POM) design pattern in UI test automation?
options: A design pattern where web pages are represented as classes and elements/actions as methods, separating test logic from page structure
A tool that automatically captures screenshots of every webpage
A CSS library for styling automated test reports
A methodology where only the home page is tested
questions.explanation: POM encapsulates page locators and interaction behaviors in dedicated classes, ensuring test scripts remain clean, reusable, and easy to maintain when UI changes.

questions.question: In the Testing Pyramid concept, which layer should contain the largest volume of tests?
options: Unit Tests
Integration Tests
End-to-End (E2E) UI Tests
Manual Exploratory Tests
questions.explanation: Unit tests are fast, cheap, and isolated, forming the wide base of the pyramid, while slow and brittle E2E UI tests form the narrow apex.

questions.question: In black-box test design, what is Boundary Value Analysis (BVA)?
options: Testing values at the extreme minimum, maximum, just inside, and just outside valid input boundaries
Testing the physical network bandwidth limits of the test server
Testing whether database foreign keys are constrained
Testing only the middle average value of an input range
questions.explanation: BVA focuses on the boundaries of input domains (e.g. 0, 1, 99, 100, 101 for a 1-100 range) where programming errors are most frequently made.

questions.question: What is the primary cause of 'flaky' automated UI tests?
options: Hard-coded fixed sleep delays (`sleep(5)`) and race conditions with dynamic asynchronous elements rather than explicit smart waits
Using CSS locators instead of XPath
Testing on Chrome instead of Firefox
Running tests on dual-monitor workstations
questions.explanation: Hard-coded sleeps fail under varying network/CPU loads; auto-waiting locators and explicit condition polling eliminate race conditions.

questions.question: In modern test frameworks like Playwright, what is 'Auto-Waiting'?
options: The framework automatically checks element visibility, stability, and enabled state before performing actions like click or type
The browser halts all JavaScript execution for 10 seconds
The test runner delays test execution until 9:00 AM
The server pauses incoming HTTP requests during test runs
questions.explanation: Playwright automatically performs actionability checks (visible, attached to DOM, stable, enabled, not obscured) before executing actions.

questions.question: What is Regression Testing?
options: Re-running functional and non-functional tests to ensure previously developed and tested software still performs correctly after a change
Testing code written in older legacy programming languages
Testing software strictly before the alpha release
Testing database backup restoration procedures
questions.explanation: Regression testing verifies that recent code commits, bug fixes, or config changes have not inadvertently broken existing working features.

questions.question: In API test automation, what does JSON Schema Validation verify?
options: That the JSON response structure, field data types, required keys, and formatting conform strictly to the expected API contract
That the JSON file is compressed with gzip
That all JSON strings are written in uppercase
That the response time was under 100ms
questions.explanation: JSON Schema validation guarantees that API payloads maintain structural integrity and correct data types, preventing contract breakage.

questions.question: What is the key difference between Load Testing and Stress Testing?
options: Load testing measures system behavior under expected normal and peak traffic; Stress testing pushes the system beyond maximum capacity to find breaking points
Stress testing only tests database CPU usage
Load testing is performed manually without tools
Stress testing tests the mental stamina of the QA team
questions.explanation: Load testing verifies performance under anticipated loads; stress testing pushes past limits to test failure modes and recovery gracefulness.

questions.question: In Pytest or unit test frameworks, what are Test Fixtures used for?
options: Providing reusable, reliable baseline context and resources (e.g. database connections, test data, browser instances) with setup/teardown logic
Fixing syntax errors in Python code automatically
Compiling test scripts into binary executables
Formatting HTML test output reports
questions.explanation: Fixtures initialize and tear down dependencies cleanly before and after test functions, ensuring test isolation and modularity.

questions.question: What is a Quality Gate in a CI/CD pipeline?
options: A set of automated threshold criteria (e.g., zero failed tests, >80% code coverage, zero high-severity security vulnerabilities) required to pass before deployment
A physical security badge scanner for server rooms
A code linter that rejects tabs in place of spaces
A manual checklist signed on paper by management
questions.explanation: Quality gates prevent low-quality, vulnerable, or failing code builds from advancing to staging or production environments.
